narrative.overview: The answer screen is a printed instruction card pinned at the workstation: paper-white surface on a slate desk, ink-black type only, and exactly one reversed plate — the verdict — carrying the screen's authority. Built for an aviation engineer reading Cyrillic technical text under bright workshop light, contrast and size are obligations, not preferences. Nothing is decorative; every colored thing is doing a job (action, selection, confirmation, verdict). The system is flat and ruled: 1px hairlines as the only separators, zero radius everywhere, integer pixel sizes only.
keyCharacteristics: Paper card on slate desk; ink-on-paper text at every level.
One reversal per screen: the verdict plate.
State as a stamp in a fixed cell (filled/hollow square), never as text or color alone.
Refusal is the same plate voice in graphite — calm, never red.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Pine is used only where the product confirms or acts; it never decorates.

rules.name: The Calm-No-Red Rule
rules.body: Refusals, unverified rows and missing sheets render in graphite/ink tones; red is not part of this system.

rules.name: The Fixed Ramp Rule
rules.body: 13/15/17 only; new surfaces pick from these steps, never invent sizes.

dos: Do verify before displaying: the «Проверено» stamp is only ever the color of a machine-checked citation.
Do keep the four pinned zones in the pinned order on every future variant of this window.
Do render refusals and absences in graphite/ink tones with the same plate geometry as confirmations.
Do use the fixed ramp (13/15/17) and integer paddings on new screens.
donts: Don't add red, orange or green traffic-light semantics to refusals or unverified rows.
Don't use Unicode glyphs or emoji as the state mark; the stamp is painted (QPainter) and stays a filled/hollow square.
Don't round any corner, soften any edge with blur, or introduce shadow.
Don't decorate with pine; if a pine thing isn't confirmable, it doesn't ship.
